correctness.rationale: The amplification R(z,θ)=(1+(1−θ)z)/(1−θz) yields |R|²−1=[−2x+(1−2θ)(x²+y²)]/[1+2θx+θ²(x²+y²)]. For two atoms a,b, imaginary-axis numerator has coefficients A,B; B≤0 is p≤(2b−1)a²/[(1−2a)b²+(2b−1)a²], and that implies A<0. The finite infinity limit equals B/(a²b²). Weighted squared analytic moduli are subharmonic, so maximum principle on left half-disks plus strict interior inequality establishes mean-square A-stability even at B=0. For p above threshold, high-frequency boundary exceeds one and continuity gives unstable Re z<0. Independently checked exact rational p*=1/10 for a=1/4,b=3/4 and coefficient vanishing. For nonconstant mean 1/2, covariance with decreasing (1+θ²y²)^{-1} gives positive F(iy)−1; expansion gives κ=2Cov(θ,θ²)>0 and implicit function gives x=κy⁴/2+O(y⁶). Finite tests alone do not prove distributional universal claims.
